bleomycin-induced lipid peroxidation is not a mere consequence of the generation of hydroxyl radical, which is the usual mechanism proposed in the literature, but it can be also a result of the formation of other reactive intermediates such as thiyl radicals.
bleomycin-Fe(II) complex in the presence of a reducing agent is able to generate thiyl radicals, which are able to isomerize the double bonds in the unsaturated phospholipids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bleomycin can be considered a prodrug, which in the presence of a suitable reducing system can induce lipid peroxidation, a well-known mechanism for the induction of apoptosis.

the bleomycin-Fe complex in combination with thiol can be used to induce lipid peroxidation and trans fatty acid formation in cell cultures and liposomes, thus opening the possibility to use bleomycin- and iron-based complexes as lipid peroxidation inducers for drug delivery and drug targeting.
the bleomycin-induced lipid peroxidation can be modulated by controlling the reagent concentration and the presence of oxygen.
